title: Replicating the 'Security vs. Innovation' Framing Analysis Across National AI-Institute Documents

original_idea.body:
# Replicating the 'Security vs. Innovation' Framing Analysis Across National AI-Institute Documents

**Problem:** A surprising recent result is divergent national framings—UK renaming AISI to 'AI Security Institute' vs. US 'CAISI' with an innovation framing. Whether this rhetorical divergence actually shows up systematically in the substance of each institute's published outputs (eval priorities, risk language, deadlines) versus being a surface label is not empirically characterized.

**Direction:** Replicate a structured content-analysis / coding methodology (the kind used for framework analysis) on a corpus of national AI-institute publications, with the twist of operationalizing 'security framing' vs. 'innovation framing' into measurable text features (risk-vs-opportunity word frequencies, presence of binding language, eval emphasis). Quantify whether the rebrands correspond to substantive divergence.

**Why it matters:** International coordination on evaluation methodology (an open problem) is harder if national institutes diverge substantively, not just rhetorically. Pure public-document text analysis, beginner-friendly NLP, no proprietary data, high counterfactual value.

**Relevant context:** Grounded in the context file's surprising result (UK 'AI Security Institute' vs. US 'CAISI' framings) and standardized content-coding methods. International Network of AI Safety Institutes provides the comparison set.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Framing word-frequency analysis has only a vague, indirect link to catastrophic-risk reduction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Beginner-friendly NLP/content coding on public documents.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused content-analysis deliverable with defined text features.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Public documents only, labs have no incentive.

novelty.reasoning: Recent surprising result; systematic discourse measurement may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Recent surprising result; systematic discourse measurement may be open.
